bib.title: BloombergGPT: A Large Language Model for Finance

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed for lineage only; figure plots not viewed (captions only).

question: Can an LLM trained on a mix of a large private financial corpus and public general-purpose data beat general LLMs on financial tasks without losing general-purpose ability?
hypothesis: Training on high-quality finance-specific data (mixed with general data) will yield better results on financial tasks while staying competitive on general benchmarks.
contributions: BloombergGPT, a 50B-parameter decoder-only LLM trained on 363B tokens of finance data (FinPile) plus 345B tokens of public data
Evaluation on public financial tasks, Bloomberg-internal tasks and standard general LLM benchmarks
Documentation of modelling choices (Unigram tokenizer, Chinchilla-guided sizing) and the Training Chronicles (Appendix C)

method.summary: A 70-layer BLOOM-style decoder-only model (50.6B parameters) was trained from scratch with a causal LM objective on a 708B-token corpus of about half Bloomberg finance text (FinPile) and half public text (Pile, C4, Wikipedia), for 569B tokens (~80% of one epoch). It was compared with GPT-NeoX 20B, OPT 66B and BLOOM 176B (GPT-3 and PaLM numbers reported from other work) using few-shot standard prompting.
method.task: next-token pretraining (causal LM) of a domain-mixed LLM; few-shot evaluation on finance and general tasks

datasets.name: FinPile (Web, News, Filings, Press, Bloomberg)
datasets.size: 363B tokens (51.27% of training); Web 298B, News 38B, Filings 14B, Press 9B, Bloomberg 5B
datasets.split: validation: July 2022 (val_future, ~105M tokens) plus last 105M tokens of training data (val_past)
datasets.source: Bloomberg archives, dated 2007-03-01 to 2022-07-31; private, not released
datasets.preprocessing: deduplicated following Lee et al. (2022a); markup, special formatting and templates stripped

datasets.name: The Pile
datasets.preprocessing: deduplicated (Lee et al., 2022a), which shrinks it substantially

datasets.name: Wikipedia (English, 1 July 2022 dump)
datasets.preprocessing: deduplicated; 3.06 characters per token, markup suspected

datasets.name: Public financial tasks (FPB, FiQA SA, Headline, NER, ConvFinQA)
datasets.size: FPB 970 test sentences; FiQA SA 235 test; Headline 2,283 test; NER 98 test sentences; ConvFinQA 1,490 conversations / 5,932 questions (dev set used)
datasets.split: own random splits for FPB, FiQA, Headline; official or dev split otherwise; few-shot examples from train
datasets.source: Malo 2014; Maia 2018; Sinha and Khandait 2020; Salinas Alvarado 2015; Chen 2022
datasets.preprocessing: FiQA discretised to negative (-1 <= x < -0.1), neutral, positive (0.1 <= x <= 1); NER drops MISC and sentences without entities

datasets.name: Bloomberg-internal sentiment (5 tasks) and NER / NER+NED (7 datasets each)
datasets.size: sentiment: up to 1,000 test examples (800 for Equity Transcript); NER: 4,000 train and 500 test per dataset
datasets.source: Bloomberg internal, annotated by 2 annotators plus a tie-breaker; private
datasets.preprocessing: NER restricted to ORG, PER, LOC; documents without entities removed

datasets.name: General benchmarks (BBH 23 tasks, ARC, CommonsenseQA, MMLU, PiQA, BoolQ, OpenBookQA, RACE, MultiRC, ReCoRD, RTE, ANLI, CB, COPA, WIC, Winograd, Winogrande, HellaSWAG, StoryCloze)
datasets.size: see Table 5: BBH 23, knowledge 5, reading comprehension 5, linguistic 9 tasks
datasets.split: official test set where labels are public, else dev; 20% test split if no official split

models.name: BloombergGPT
models.architecture: decoder-only causal transformer, BLOOM-based, ALiBi, GELU, tied input/output embeddings, extra LayerNorm after embeddings, pre-LN blocks
models.init_from: random init, N(0, sqrt(1/(3D)) = 0.006588); second FFN layer and attention output rescaled by 1/sqrt(2L)
models.tokenizer: Unigram, byte-level, trained on The Pile via 22 domains x 256 chunks merged; pretokenization regex [ A-Za-z]+|[0-9]|[^A-Za-z0-9]+
models.context: 2,048 tokens in training (ALiBi allows longer at inference)

models.name: BLOOM
models.architecture: decoder-only, same architecture and software stack

other.note: numbers reported from Brown et al. 2020, not rerun
BBH numbers taken from the BBH paper

training.lr_schedule: cosine decay with linear warmup; later manual cuts: x2/3 at step 115,500, x1/2 at 129,900, x1/2 at 137,100
training.batch_size: 1,024 sequences (2.1M tokens) for the first 7,200 steps, then 2,048 sequences (4.2M tokens)
training.steps: 139,200 steps for the selected checkpoint (run ended at 146,000)
training.seq_len: 2,048 tokens, documents concatenated with <|endoftext|> and chunked
training.precision: BF16 forward/backward, FP32 parameter storage and update; FP32 for fused softmax, loss softmax and ALiBi matrices (stored BF16)
training.weight_decay: 0.1 (not applied to LayerNorm gain; bug fixed in v2.0)
training.hardware: 64 p4d.24xlarge instances = 512 NVIDIA A100 40GB on AWS SageMaker; ZeRO stage 3 via SageMaker Model Parallelism, MiCS, activation checkpointing per layer, fused masked-causal-softmax kernel; model sharded across 128 GPUs with 4 copies
training.compute: 2.36e23 FLOPs total; 102 TFLOPs average per GPU; budget 1.3M A100-40GB GPU hours
training.seeds: inferred: a single final run; v2.0 used a different seed from v1.x, no seed count stated

other.validation_cadence: validation every 300 steps; training loss logged every 5 steps, smoothed with alpha 0.001
other.scaling_fit: Chinchilla approach 1: 52.993B params / 1111.112B tokens; approach 2: 49.753B / 1175.766B; 0.75 x 1.3M GPU hours used because activation checkpointing adds 0.33x; ~30% of budget kept as buffer
other.shape_rule: D = exp(5.039) exp(0.0555 L) (Levine et al. 2020) gave L=70, D=7510, rounded to 7680 for 40 heads x 192
other.tokenizer_vocab_search: vocab 25,000 to 550,000 compared on encoded C4 size; optimum 125,000 rounded to 2^17
other.interventions: v0 curriculum learning (abandoned), v1.x gradient-norm elbow at ~12k steps (4 failed fixes), v2.0 conservative restart with ~10 changes, then v2.1-v2.6 LR/dropout/weight-decay variants after validation loss stalled at step 115,500

inference.decoding: greedy for generative tasks; likelihood-based classification (regular, calibration, or length normalisation; best per model and task reported) when candidates are given
inference.samples: Shots resampled per test example to reduce variance; no seeds or repeat runs stated
inference.prompting: standard few-shot prompting, no task descriptions, no chain-of-thought; shots: 5 (FPB, FiQA SA, Headline, internal sentiment), 20 (NER, internal NER and NER+NED), 3 (BBH), 1 (knowledge, reading, linguistic, ConvFinQA), 5 (MMLU)

other.long_document_loss: sliding window with half-window context for held-out bits-per-byte; tokens beyond the first 2,048 have at least 1,024 tokens of context

metrics.name: bits per byte
metrics.definition: held-out loss on a temporally held-out FinPile set

metrics.definition: F1 weighted by label support (sentiment, Headline)

metrics.name: win rate (WR)

eval.protocol: Authors run GPT-NeoX, OPT and BLOOM themselves with identical inputs; GPT-3 and PaLM numbers are reported from other papers. Shot counts for public finance tasks were chosen so average performance across models was best. One setup per dataset; no error bars or significance tests stated.

limits: No ablation: no public-only or finance-only twin and no same-model run with a different tokenizer, so the stated ranking of causes is untested.
Model weights, FinPile and the internal benchmarks are not released; internal results cannot be checked.
Internal task text likely appears in FinPile, so the authors concede possible contamination (Section 5.3.2).
Shot counts for public finance tasks were chosen to maximise average performance across models, and the best of three classification methods is reported per model and task; no error bars or seeds.
Compute is only partly comparable across the cohort (BLOOM data one-third English, OPT repeated data).
Toxicity and bias were not measured; effects of the tokenizer on the model left to future work.
Training ended at ~80% of one epoch, with budget nearly spent; longer training might have helped.
The Chinchilla law is tokenizer-specific and transfer across tokenizers is open (footnote 1).
LLaMA could not be compared (no third-party results or weights, footnote 2). Training data ends July 2022.
